Let
\[
p=2ht-s^2-3h^2s\in k[h,s,t].
\]
Then the center is
\[
\boxed{
Z(R)=k\bigl[h^5,\;h(2ht-s^2-3h^2s),\;(2ht-s^2-3h^2s)^5,\;xy\bigr].
}
\]

**Solution.** Let \(A=k[h,s,t]\). The relations say \(R=A[x,y;\sigma,\sigma^{-1}]\), with \(x a=\sigma(a)x\), \(y a=\sigma^{-1}(a)y\), where
\[
\sigma(h)=\zeta h,\qquad
\sigma(s)=\zeta^2(s+h^2),\qquad
\sigma(t)=\zeta^3(t+hs+2h^3).
\]
Indeed the displayed formulas for \(y\) give \(\sigma^{-1}\), and \(xy=yx\).

First compute the \(\sigma\)-invariants of \(A\). A direct substitution gives
\[
\sigma(p)=\zeta^4p.
\]
Thus \(h^5\), \(hp\), and \(p^5\) are fixed by \(\sigma\).

To see these are all invariants, localize at \(h\), and set
\[
u=\frac{s}{h^2},\qquad q=\frac{p}{2h^4}.
\]
Then
\[
\sigma(h)=\zeta h,\qquad \sigma(u)=u+1,\qquad \sigma(q)=q.
\]
Hence \(\sigma^5\) fixes \(h,q\) and sends \(u\mapsto u+5\). Since \(\operatorname{char}k=0\), a polynomial invariant under \(u\mapsto u+5\) is independent of \(u\). Therefore every invariant in \(A_h\) lies in \(k[h,h^{-1},q]\). Invariance under \(\sigma\) then forces only powers \(h^{5m}\), so
\[
(A_h)^\sigma=k[h^5,h^{-5},q].
\]
Since \(q=p/(2h^4)\), intersecting with \(A=k[h,s,t]\) gives precisely the span of monomials
\[
h^a p^b\quad\text{with}\quad a,b\ge 0,\qquad a+4b\equiv 0\pmod 5.
\]
Writing \(b=5c+r\), \(0\le r\le 4\), this congruence gives \(a=r+5\ell\), so
\[
h^a p^b=(h^5)^\ell (hp)^r(p^5)^c.
\]
Thus
\[
A^\sigma=k[h^5,hp,p^5].
\]

Now let \(z\in Z(R)\). Since \(R\) has \(A\)-basis \(\{x^m y^n:m,n\ge0\}\), write
\[
z=\sum_{m,n} a_{mn}x^m y^n,\qquad a_{mn}\in A.
\]
For \(a\in A\),
\[
x^m y^n a=\sigma^{m-n}(a)x^m y^n.
\]
Commuting with \(h,s,t\) forces \(\sigma^{m-n}=\mathrm{id}\) on \(A\). But
\[
\sigma^r(h)=\zeta^r h,
\]
so \(r\) must be divisible by \(5\), and then
\[
\sigma^r(s)=s+r h^2,
\]
which equals \(s\) only when \(r=0\). Hence \(m=n\). Therefore every central element has the form
\[
z=\sum_n a_n(xy)^n.
\]
The element \(xy\) is central, because
\[
xy\,a=x\sigma^{-1}(a)y=a\,xy
\]
for all \(a\in A\), and \(xy=yx\). Finally, commuting with \(x\) forces
\[
\sigma(a_n)=a_n,
\]
so \(a_n\in A^\sigma\). Hence
\[
Z(R)=A^\sigma[xy]
=k[h^5,hp,p^5,xy],
\]
with \(p=2ht-s^2-3h^2s\).
